episodes.title: Starlink Mini 2, Starmind solar contract, Businesses in ChatGPT
episodes.dek: Previous 24 hours: Starlink Mini 2 portable, SpaceX 100 GW solar for Starmind, OpenAI Business Hub and Agents, other labs quiet.

sections.headline: Wednesday morning roundup
sections.dek: The previous twenty-four hours in AI and space.
paragraphs: Good morning. This is Leo Ward with Good Morning AI. Wednesday, November eleventh. The previous twenty-four hours in AI and space.

sections.headline: Starlink Mini 2 and Starmind solar
sections.dek: Portable Starlink announced; major solar equipment contract for satellites.
sections.reaction: No new launch in the window.
paragraphs: SpaceX and xAI: Starlink introduced Mini 2, the next-generation portable Starlink. Get up to 4.5 hours of connectivity on a single charge with the quick-swap battery, or plug in with USB-C. With built-in Wi-Fi, all you need is a clear view of the sky to get online in 60 seconds. Preorders are now open by invitation in the US. Elon Musk shared it, calling it portable, lightning-fast Internet that works anywhere on Earth where Starlink is legal. SpaceX signed a major supply contract with SINGULUS to create a durable option for advanced solar cell manufacturing to support more than 100 GW of equipment as they accelerate the production of Starmind satellites in Bastrop, Texas. Elon commented that SpaceX has ordered 100 GW per year of HJT solar manufacturing equipment from Singulus in Germany. This is for Starmind to create a sentient sun. Super Heavy moved to the launch pad at Starbase. Booster 22 is the first Super Heavy V3 booster planned to return to the launch site for catch and was used for final catch testing upon arrival, including a suspended squeeze test at catch height. No new launch in the window.

sections.headline: Businesses in ChatGPT
sections.dek: Beta launch of Business Hub and Business Agents.
paragraphs: OpenAI announced Businesses in ChatGPT, now in beta. Businesses can claim their business, manage their information, and get insights on how people engage with them. Eligible businesses can also build a Business Agent to answer customers’ questions and help them explore what they offer. They are also turning lessons from defending OpenAI into practical tools for customers, with a live keynote on Cyber at the Frontier scheduled for Thursday.
